nora: FYI - some customers reported fails mounting snapshots. Error looks like KMS denied when trying to unwrap DEK for an HSM-backed CMK.
pete: paste the log snippet
nora: ```
2026-03-30T21:11:02Z ERROR restore: dek_unwrap: rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = caller lacks cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
2026-03-30T21:11:02Z INFO snapshot=tenant-sage-20260315 restore=rs-901
```
kms-bot: IAM audit: cryptoKey IAM change on projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/backups/cryptoKeys/hsm-db-key removed members: serviceAccount:uploader@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com at 2026-03-30T20:45:00Z
jasmin: that uploader SA used to have decrypt via a cross-project grant we set up for historical reasons (legacy backup import). The RBAC cleanup removed a broad project role and the key policy never had an explicit cross-project binding.
ops-eli: interesting wrinkle: because this is an HSM-backed CMK with strict keyPolicy, we can't add arbitrary members without customer consent in some cases. Check if the key is customer-supplied and whether it has an external binding block.
pete: running `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy hsm-db-key --keyring=backups --location=global` now shows only `backup-decryptor@redwood-prod` and `ops-kms@redwood.com` group. uploader missing.
nora: immediate mitigation options: 1) request temporary decrypt grant for uploader SA (fast) 2) run the restore job under backup-decryptor SA (requires switching restore executor) 3) if key policy disallows adding uploader, we must run under decryptor SA or rekey (bad).
jasmin: because it's HSM-backed and cross-project grants were used historically, I suspect the original import used a service account in a different project. Our RBAC prune removed that link. We should prefer option 2 and avoid adding uploader to the key policy.
ops-eli: I temporarily kicked the restore to run under backup-decryptor SA (we have a flag on the restore controller `--run-as=backup-decryptor`) and the snapshot mounted fine. Verified DB integrity check passed.
pete: good. root cause: RBAC cleanup removed broad role that indirectly allowed uploader to decrypt via cross-project grant; key IAM lacked explicit binding.
nora: action items: (SEC) map all keys with HSM/CMK properties and identify any workflows relying on cross-project or implicit grants (assignee: jasmin). (ENG) add a config toggle so restore-controller can switch SA at runtime for specific snapshots (assignee: ops-eli). (SRE) add pre-merge test: after IAM PR merge run quick `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy` for backup keys and fail CI if decrypt bindings for any known pipeline SA were removed without mapped replacement (assignee: pete). (SEC/LEGAL) review customer-key policies for HSM keys to ensure we don't violate consent when adding members (assignee: jasmin).
jasmin: follow-up: I'll prepare a short doc listing which HSM-backed keys are customer-managed and which we may not modify; will propose a policy to always run restores under a dedicated decryptor SA for those keys.
nora: also adding an audit alert for any removal from backup key IAMs that affect known pipeline SAs (low-noise filter: only alert on removals).
ops-eli: I've opened ENGSEC-9133 "HSM CMK: migrate restore executions to backup-decryptor SA and enumerate cross-project grants" and linked logs + CI reproduction.
pete: small playbook note: before RBAC prune, run `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy --location=global --keyring=backups --format=json` and also check key `purpose` and `protectionLevel` fields to catch HSM CMKs. If HSM, route to manual review.
ora: thanks all. Will keep the temporary run-as change until eng PR lands. :thumbsup:
